properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 8 at 5:58AM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
At 558 AM PDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Cheney, moving northeast at 50 mph.

HAZARD...Winds in excess of 30 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Spokane, Spokane Valley, Coeur d'Alene, Post Falls, Cheney, Rathdrum,
Liberty Lake, Millwood, Hauser, Green Acres, Otis Orchards-East
Farms, Trentwood, Otis Orchards, Dishman, Huetter, State Line, Newman
Lake, Marshall, Opportunity, and Veradale.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 90 in Washington between mile markers 281 and 299.
Interstate 90 in Idaho between mile markers 0 and 10.
U.S. Highway 195 in Washington between mile markers 86 and 95.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

properties.description:

Eastern Norfolk MA, Eastern Plymouth MA, Barnstable MA and
Nantucket MA Counties.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 8 at 7:49AM CDT until July 8 at 10:00AM CDT by NWS Fort Worth TX
properties.description:
FFWFWD

The National Weather Service in Fort Worth has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Hopkins County in north central Texas...

* Until 1000 AM CDT.

* At 749 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over eastern Hopkins County, mainly between Sulphur
Bluff and Saltillo. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have fallen.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Rapid rises
to the White Oak Bayou and its tributaries are also ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Saltillo, Pine Forest, Weaver, Flora and Dike.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

properties.areaDesc: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 8 at 7:51PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Super Typhoon Bavi (09W) is currently centered near 17N133E, roughly
630 miles northwest of Yap and 680 miles north of Palau. Maximum
sustained winds are 155 mph. Yap and Palau continue to face impacts
from elevated northwest swells emanating from STY Bavi and the
trailing monsoon pattern.

Hazardous seas up to 16 feet will continue tonight at Yap, and up to
14 feet at Palau, generated by an elevated northwest swell from STY
Bavi, and from elevated southwest monsoon swell and wind waves.
Surging southwest winds of 20 to 30 knots with gusts to 35 knots will
continue tonight, especially near any heavier showers, contributing
to hazardous sea conditions through the next few days. Inter-island
travel will be dangerous. As Bavi continues to pull away toward the
northwest over the next few days, the monsoon pattern will shift
northwest with it, and winds, seas, and surf will gradually subside.
Even so, hazardous surf conditions will continue through at least
Friday afternoon, associated with the elevated swells.

For more information on Super Typhoon Bavi, please refer to the
Public Advisory issued by the National Weather Service under WMO
header WTPQ31 PGUM and the Tropical Cyclone Warning issued by the
Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW.

evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and

conditioner to 75 degrees or above.

Hazards include sneaker waves, strong rip currents, and large
breaking waves. High tide flooding of lots, parks, and roads
with only isolated road closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 0.9 ft above normal (6.7 ft MLLW) at 7:25 PM

above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 9:11 PM 7/11, 1.7 ft above normal

11:55 PM 7/14, 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 12:48 AM
7/16. These predictions include both astronomical tides and
roughly 3-6 inches of additional water mainly from a combination
of thermal expansion and accumulated sea level rise since the
tidal datum was established (1983-2001). High tide varies up to
90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through

unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

IDAHO ZONES...

.Scattered thunderstorms are expected again across southern Idaho
south of the Snake Basin to the Nevada border Wednesday
afternoon. Expect gusty and erratic winds up to 50 mph in the
vicinity of these thunderstorms.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Idaho, Fire Weather Zones 423 Owyhee
Mountains and 426 Southern Highlands.

* TIMING...From 1 PM to 8 PM MDT Wednesday.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Scattered coverage with abundant lightning.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusty erratic winds up to 50 to 60 mph.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will occur shortly.

The Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy
(EGLE) has issued an Air Quality Alert for July 8, 2026, for
elevated levels of ozone in west and southwest Michigan.

Pollutants  within those areas are expected to be in the Unhealthy
for Sensitive Groups range.

The Air Quality Alert is in effect for  the following Michigan
counties:

Muskegon, Ottawa, Kent, Allegan, Barry, Van Buren

Warm temperatures, ample sunlight and southwest winds will mix with
pollutants to produce surface-level Ozone in west and southwest
Michigan.

It is recommended that, when possible, you avoid strenuous
outdoor activities, especially those with heart disease and
respiratory conditions like asthma.

dizziness, or burning in nose, throat, and eyes. People and
businesses are urged to avoid activities which can lead to ozone
formation.

These activities include:

Refueling vehicles or topping off when refueling;

Using gasoline powered lawn equipment;

Using charcoal lighter fluid.

Positive activities include:

Driving less;

Telecommuting;

Delaying or combining errands.

properties.areaDesc: Grand Canyon Country
properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued July 7 at 1:23AM MST until July 11 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions below 4000 feet, with daytime
temperatures ranging from 101 to 104 degrees at Havasupai Gardens
and 111 to 114 degrees at Phantom Ranch.

* WHERE...Lower elevations of the Grand Canyon.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Most individuals will be at risk for heat-related
illnesses without effective cooling or adequate hydration,
especially with prolonged outdoor exposure.
properties.instruction:
This warning is reserved for only the hottest days of the year and is
issued when temperatures are expected to rise to dangerous levels.

Day hikers on Bright Angel Trail should descend no farther than 1 1/2
miles from the upper trailhead. Between the hours of 10 AM and 4 PM,
hikers should be out of the canyon or at Havasupai Gardens or Bright
Angel campgrounds, physical activity is discouraged. All hikers
should have adequate gear, including a wide-brimmed hat, sunscreen,
salty snacks, sufficient water, and electrolyte mix. Doubling your
calorie intake helps maintain your energy.

Hike smart.

Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke.
Anyone overcome by heat should be moved to a cool and shaded
location. Heat stroke is an emergency! Call 9 1 1.
